title: Drummers and keeping steady time
summary: Drummers with Johnny Brown including Faisal and Dave Ernest, and why a drummer must not lag or rush.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Good drummers? Did they have good drummers in those days?
Oh yeah, they had what you call right time drummers.

See, when we first started from Johnny Brown, with Johnny Brown we had a drummer by the name of Faisal. He died early and then we got a fella by the name of Dave. Now I can't think of his last name right now, he had a brother called Ernest. Duck Ernest?
Hmm? Duck Ernest was his brother?
Duck Ernest was his brother, yeah. Half of different fathers.

Well he must be Dave Ernest. Dave was a good drummer too, Dave was. He had to be good because he had to really, he changed him up if he wasn't good. That is, you have to keep that rhythm, you can't increase, you don't want no drummer going to increase, you don't want no drummer going to lag. You got to be right on the beat, you know? Like that, you play more easy, it's more easy on everybody. You get some drummers, they, they kind of lag just a section or a fraction of you, just keep, they drag you back, you see? Mm-hm. We started hitting our foot there with no reason to come up on that drum a little bit. And if he had to keep it going, I would get rid of him. He couldn't lag. All that started right here in the city. Putting a little more to it, a little more to it. And I think I could, with the chamber, not bragging on myself, I could play a whole lot of them. I could play, by playing the trumpet and had talent for music, I could put a whole lot in that, in the piece, you see, like that.
